summary.where_we_are: Tuesday 19:37 SGT / 07:37 ET, US pre-market (open 21:30 SGT), SGX closed with the STI down 1.4%. The Fed's two-day meeting starts today; the decision lands Thursday 02:00 SGT. I could not verify any top-tier US data print at 20:30 SGT tonight.
summary.macro_attribution: The 10-year Treasury yield moved most: it crossed 5% for the first time since 2023 and touched 5.04% this morning, the highest since 2007, with oil the push behind it (Brent above $105 after Saudi Arabia shut its East-West pipeline); the VIX at 17 with a calm term structure has not moved. The big-tech and whole-market leans depend on that yield; the chip lean is positioning after Monday and does not.
what_happened: Chips had their worst day since July on Monday (Philadelphia semiconductor index -5.9%; SK hynix ADR -7%, Micron, Intel, Marvell -4% or worse) after Anthropic's Dario Amodei, OpenAI's Sam Altman and Elon Musk called for slowing frontier-model development; Trump dismissed it on Sunday (CNBC, Sep 14). SOXX volume ran 1.57x normal (tape). A slower model cadence is not a capex cut, which is the whole bounce case.

Tuesday pre-market: 16 of 18 chip names are up, median +1.0% (tape). Equipment leads, and on real volume: Soitec +4.4% and Aixtron +2.1% in Paris and Frankfurt regular trade, ASML +3.0% pre-market with RSI 36 and 9% below its 50-day average. The cluster sits 0.8% below its 50-day with no name overbought: a rebound from below, not an extension. US pre-market prints carry no volume, so the bounce is thin until the open.

Big tech is 0 for 5 pre-market (Microsoft -1.2%, Palantir -1.5%, Meta -0.5% with RSI 71) and sits 10.5% above its 50-day, the most stretched group on the tape, into a 10-year at 5.04% (tape; CNBC, Sep 15).

A quarter-point Fed hike to 3.75-4.00% on Wednesday is close to fully priced (Investing.com, Sep 15 03:58 ET); a day earlier the same outlet had it as merely more likely than not, so the market repriced toward a hike as oil and yields rose.

Singapore banks fell 2.7% today (OCBC -2.7% on 1.6x volume, UOB -2.7%, DBS -1.0%; tape) with no headline I could find in four searches. The timing matches the global bond selloff. Standing risk on DBS: the S$1.3 billion 1MDB-linked claim announced Sep 9 (catalysts.json).
